newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU informal stability council for EMU likely-Zalm.
newsitem.headline: EU informal stability council for EMU likely-Zalm.

text.p: EU finance ministers on Monday discussed plans to set up an informal stability council to coordinate policy after the launch of monetary union, Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm told a news conference after a meeting of EU finance ministers.
He said that there was a consensus among member states that such an informal club would be set up although there was no consensus that it was necessary.

"The stability council is an informal club bringing together countries in the euro zone. It should not be a counterweight to the European Central Bank. It should be a complement to the European Central Bank." Zalm said.
"This club should not have any power to take decisions," Zalm said through an interpreter.
He noted that it was impossible to prevent a group of member states getting together informally to discuss matters of common interest.

Asked whether that meant there was now a consensus to set up the council, first proposed by France, he said "There is a consensus to say that something of this kind will be set up. There is no consensus on the need to set it up."
Asked whether the stability council would have any role in fixing currency policy, he said: "This council will have no competence."

Currency policy would be a matter for either all 15 finance ministers or the European Central Bank. "If ministers meet informally they can discuss anything that comes into their heads including their weather forecasts for the next day," he said.

EU diplomats said some of the smaller countries in the EU were angered by an agreement between France and Germany to set up such a council which they fear could be used to enhance the powers of the bigger countries in the future currency zone. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
